title: Yasmine: Name Meaning, Origin & Personality
summary: Yasmine is a soft, elegant name that means jasmine, the white flower known for its sweet perfume. It is loved in the Arab world and in Europe alike.
origin: Yasmine comes from the Persian word 'yasaman', the name of the jasmine flower. It entered Arabic as ياسمين and from there travelled into French, English and many other languages, often spelled Jasmine or Yasmin. Jasmine flowers have long been planted in gardens and courtyards across the Mediterranean and the Middle East, where their scent fills the evening air, so the name carries a feeling of beauty, peace and home.
personality: A Yasmine is often imagined as gentle, graceful and warm, with a natural charm that makes people feel welcome. Like the flower, she is thought to be delicate on the outside but strong and lasting inside. Many associate the name with creativity, a love of beautiful things and a sensitive, caring heart. Yasmines are also seen as sociable and optimistic, bringing a light, sweet atmosphere wherever they go.
popularity: Yasmine and its spellings are popular in Morocco, Algeria, Tunisia, Egypt and the Gulf countries, as well as in France, Belgium and Canada. In English-speaking countries the form Jasmine is more common, while Yasmin is frequent in Germany and the United Kingdom.

faq.q: What does the name Yasmine mean?
faq.ans: Yasmine means 'jasmine flower'. It symbolises beauty, sweetness and grace.
It is very common in Arabic as ياسمين, but its origin is Persian. Arabic then spread it to many other languages.

faq.q: What is the difference between Yasmine, Yasmin and Jasmine?
faq.ans: They are the same name with different spellings. Yasmine is common in French-speaking and Arab countries, Yasmin in Germany and the UK, and Jasmine in English.

faq.q: Which nicknames go well with Yasmine?
faq.ans: Popular nicknames are Yas, Mina and Yassou. Families often choose the one that sounds best in their own language.
